findings.message: ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS is parsed with two separate jq subprocess invocations (one for `.inputs.review_report`, one for `.inputs.gate_aggregator_result`) on the same file; a single `jq` call with two outputs or a `read` from a single invocation would halve the subprocess cost here, which runs on every non-misconfigured invocation.

For the `auto_unless_flagged` policy when the gate verdict is not `pass` and a review_report exists whose `merge_readiness` is not `needs_attention`, `merge_readiness` is extracted from the same file by both the upfront block guard (`_rr_readiness` local to that block) and then again by the `auto_unless_flagged` branch (`_auf_readiness`); the first read's result is not reused, so a redundant jq subprocess is spawned on this code path.

In `_pr_delivery_write_result`, the `_draft` normalisation (`[[ "$_draft" == "true" ]] || _draft="false"`) executes unconditionally before the `[[ -z "$_out_dir" ]] && return 1` guard; the normalisation is wasted work on every call where `_out_dir` is empty and the function exits immediately after.

The `_pr_delivery_write_result` helper emits `draft` both at the top level of the result envelope and inside `data`; the ADR contract reserves the top-level for `result_contract`, `verdict`, `disposition`, `reason`, and `data`, so the top-level `draft` is schema pollution that could confuse strict consumers or schema validators — the old golden (written by pr-open) had `draft` only under `data`.

The `disposition` string read from the child plugin's result file (`merge-result.json` or `pr-result.json`) is passed through directly to the parent's v2 result without validating it against ADR-054's vocabulary; a child that writes a non-standard or empty disposition propagates unchecked into the engine's result table.

`stage_signal_begin` is installed at line 133, after the dry-run guard (lines 122–130); a SIGTERM that arrives during the dry-run path's `atomic_write` call will not trigger `_pr_delivery_on_signal`, leaving no result file — the dry-run path therefore has no signal protection despite `_PR_DELIVERY_ARTIFACTS_DIR` being set at line 84.

When pr-open returns `verdict=blocked`, the v2 result unconditionally writes `reason="review_signal_missing"` regardless of `_po_reason` captured from pr-open's result file; if pr-open ever blocks for a distinguishable reason, the actual reason is silently discarded (only the stage summary retains it via `${_po_reason:-blocked}`).

The `_mk_si` helper constructs ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS JSON via `printf '%s'` with file paths; any path that contains JSON-special characters (double quotes, backslashes, newlines) will silently produce invalid JSON and cause the block guard to silently skip input resolution — `jq -n --arg` should be used instead.

`_pr_delivery_write_result` emits `draft` at the top level of the result object (line 49) in addition to inside `data` (line 50); ADR-054's v2 envelope schema defines `{result_contract, verdict, disposition, reason, data}` — plugin-specific fields belong under `data`, and the issue's SPEC-16 only specifies `data.draft`, not a top-level `draft` key.

The new golden drops `data.pr_number` and `data.issue` that pr-open previously populated; the issue specifies `data.pr_url` and `data.draft` for SPEC-16 but does not ask for removing these downstream-visible fields, and the change does so implicitly because pr-delivery now writes its own result rather than forwarding pr-open's.

The description update removes the note "plan.json/design.md are accepted as optional inputs (reserved for future PR-body composition)" — this documented an intentional placeholder not consumed by the one-shot implementation, and its removal is editorial cleanup not asked for by the issue.

The `_mk_si` helper and several inline test fixtures construct JSON via `printf '...%s...' "$path"`, which produces malformed JSON if any path contains a double-quote, backslash, or newline; `jq -n --arg key "$val"` would be safe.

The disposition value read from `merge-result.json` (and analogously from `pr-result.json`) is passed through to `_pr_delivery_write_result` without validating against the ADR-054 allowed disposition vocabulary; a compromised delegate could inject an arbitrary string into the `disposition` field of pr-delivery's own v2 result.

`_PR_DELIVERY_ARTIFACTS_DIR` is initialised to the empty string at source time; if `_pr_delivery_on_signal` fires before `pr_stage_run` or `_pr_stage_run_inner` sets it to a real path, `_pr_delivery_write_result` silently returns 1 (the empty-dir guard) and no interrupted result file is written — the contract breach is not surfaced to the caller.

The manifest declares three events (pr.delivery.blocked, pr.delivery.opened, pr.delivery.dry_run) under provides.events — which ADR-001 defines as events the plugin actually emits — but the plugin never emits any of them; the only emit_event call (line 248) fires plugin.result, not pr.delivery.blocked, leaving every monitoring, alerting, or audit trail wired to pr.delivery.* permanently dark.

stage_signal_begin is installed at line 133, after both the block-guard (lines 106-120) and dry-run path (lines 123-130); a SIGTERM arriving while jq reads the review_report or gate artifact in the block-guard section leaves no pr-result.json on disk — the unguarded window is narrower than before the change (previously the entire function was unprotected) but is non-zero because jq performs file I/O.

draft appears at the v2 result top level AND nested under data.draft in _pr_delivery_write_result; ADR-054 §4 defines the envelope as {result_contract, verdict, disposition, reason, data} with plugin-specific detail under data, so the top-level draft field is outside the declared schema — confirmed by the updated golden which also carries draft twice.

The updated golden removes data.pr_number, data.issue, and data.status from pr-result.json (fields previously written by pr-open and now replaced by pr-delivery's own v2 result); any reporting, summary, or downstream tooling that reads data.pr_number from this artifact will silently receive empty — rollback to v1 restores the old fields, so recovery is straightforward.
